bug_description.original: A bug in glibc/regex/msan causes regexec to return 0 but not initialize pmatch.
bug_description.normalized: On the witnessed FILE_REGEX path, `magiccheck` allocates stack `regmatch_t pmatch` and calls `file_regexec`. The vulnerable wrapper forwards that output buffer to `regexec` without clearing it first. In the staged glibc/MSan environment, `regexec` returns success but leaves `pmatch.rm_so` and `pmatch.rm_eo` undefined. `magiccheck` then rewrites `ms->search.s`, `ms->search.offset`, and `ms->search.rm_len` from those fields, and the later `mprint` call in `match` consumes that poisoned regex-match state, triggering MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value.

source.code: ms->search.s = buf; ms->search.s_len = last - buf; ms->search.offset = offset; ms->search.rm_len = 0;
source.description: The crashing FILE_REGEX path materializes its regex search window by aliasing an attacker-controlled byte slice into `ms->search` and recording its length and starting offset.
source.value_from: The staged witness file `poc` is the exact 12-byte blob `50 2a 4d 18 00 00 00 00 50 36 4d 18` (hex). On the observed stack path, soft-magic matching recurses once through `FILE_INDIRECT`, and the inner FILE_REGEX `mcopy` arm aliases a slice of those witness bytes into `ms->search` for regex execution.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MSan crash site. The call into `mprint` for the FILE_REGEX entry consumes the regex match state that `magiccheck` previously rewrote from uninitialized `pmatch` fields.

root_cause.code: return regexec(&rx->rx, str, nmatch, pmatch, eflags);
root_cause.description: The wrapper passes caller-owned `pmatch` to libc regex without initializing it first. The fix adds `memset(pmatch, 0, nmatch * sizeof(*pmatch));` before `regexec`, so successful matches no longer rely on the C library to define every `regmatch_t` field.

parser_admitted.code: m = file_softmagic(ms, ubuf, nb, NULL, NULL, BINTEST, looks_text);
parser_admitted.description: After earlier container checks, the witness enters soft-magic matching on the attacker-controlled buffer. The observed stack shows this path taking a `FILE_INDIRECT` recursion before the crashing FILE_REGEX evaluation.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant poisoned value is the stack match buffer `pmatch`. MemorySanitizer attributes the uninitialized value to this allocation in `magiccheck` when the later regex call leaves the structure untouched.

fine_trace.code: ms->search.s = buf; ms->search.s_len = last - buf; ms->search.offset = offset; ms->search.rm_len = 0;
fine_trace.note: On the witnessed inner FILE_REGEX path, `mcopy` aliases the attacker-controlled search window into `ms->search`, recording its pointer, length, and starting offset. This is the first project statement that materializes the exact input slice later passed to `regexec` and later printed.

The FILE_REGEX arm allocates stack match buffer `pmatch`, but this declaration does not initialize any field. MSan's origin report attributes the poisoned value to this stack allocation in `magiccheck`.

fine_trace.code: size_t slen = ms->search.s_len; if (slen != 0) { copy = CAST(char *, malloc(slen)); memcpy(copy, ms->search.s, slen); copy[--slen] = '\0'; search = copy; } else { search = CCAST(char *, ""); copy = NULL; }
fine_trace.note: Before the regex call, `magiccheck` derives the `search` argument from the previously materialized `ms->search` window. The source either copies that window into a temporary NUL-terminated buffer when `slen != 0` or uses `""` when `slen == 0`; the staged artifacts do not disambiguate which arm fired, only that the resulting `search` pointer is what gets passed to `file_regexec`.

fine_trace.code: return regexec(&rx->rx, str, nmatch, pmatch, eflags);
fine_trace.note: Root cause. `file_regexec` forwards caller-owned output buffer `pmatch` straight into `regexec` without the zero-fill added by the fix. On the witnessed glibc/MSan path, `regexec` returns success to its caller but does not define `pmatch.rm_so` or `pmatch.rm_eo`.

fine_trace.code: case 0: ms->search.s += (int)pmatch.rm_so; ms->search.offset += (size_t)pmatch.rm_so; ms->search.rm_len = (size_t)(pmatch.rm_eo - pmatch.rm_so); v = 0;
fine_trace.note: Because `rc == 0`, the FILE_REGEX arm treats `pmatch` as valid and rewrites shared search state from `pmatch.rm_so` and `pmatch.rm_eo`. If those fields were left undefined, `ms->search.s`, `ms->search.offset`, and `ms->search.rm_len` all become poisoned before control returns to `match()`.

fine_trace.code: v = file_signextend(ms, m, v); switch (m->reln) { ... } return matched;
fine_trace.note: After regex handling falls through, `magiccheck` sign-extends `v` and applies the rule's `m->reln` comparison before returning `matched`. The staged artifacts do not identify the exact comparison arm, but the witnessed sink proves this return was nonzero on the crashing path because `match()` reached its printing case rather than `case 0`.

The same rule evaluation takes the successful `magiccheck` branch rather than the `case 0` rejection path, so `match()` proceeds into its print logic for this FILE_REGEX entry instead of `continue`-ing.

MSan sink. The call into `mprint` for the FILE_REGEX rule consumes the poisoned `ms->search` state produced from uninitialized `pmatch` fields, and the sanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value at this call site.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The MSan origin is the stack allocation of `pmatch` in `magiccheck`; the patched project-side obligation is the adjacent `file_regexec` wrapper, which must initialize that caller-owned buffer before delegating to `regexec`.

format.name: Exact 12-byte witness blob for magic_fuzzer
format.contract: The available evidence establishes only the exact witness file: 12 bytes `50 2a 4d 18 00 00 00 00 50 36 4d 18` (hex). In the staged run, this blob drives soft-magic matching through a `FILE_INDIRECT` recursion into a FILE_REGEX rule, where `magiccheck` builds a `search` pointer from `ms->search` and then calls `file_regexec(&rx, (const char *)search, 1, &pmatch, 0)`. On the witnessed glibc/MSan path, `regexec` returns 0 while leaving `pmatch` uninitialized, and the later `mprint` call reports MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value. The staged artifacts do not establish whether `magiccheck` took the `slen != 0` copy arm or the `slen == 0` empty-string arm, and they do not justify a broader file-format contract.
